mxCell.value: Restaurant Rush | Stage 3 | Turn 7 — VIP arrival, seating, discounted ordering and first preparation

Use case: seat VIP customer 3, take the Pasta order and prepare its first unit during Happy Hour. Starting conditions: currentTurn = 7; this turn has not started; table 1 is free; Happy Hour is unused. Player selects Yes, then Host → Waiter → Chef. Scope: customer 3; routine UI queries, getters and nonessential validation are omitted. Other customers may interact during this turn.
1. Arrival and Happy Hour
«create» VIPCustomer(3)
New customer: id = 3, status = WAITING, satisfaction = 100, order = null. Arrival is processed before Happy Hour bonuses.
[activateHappyHour = true] — selected in this use case
[happyHourTurnsRemaining > 0 and (customer3.status = WAITING or customer3.status = SEATED)]
State: customer3 is WAITING with satisfaction = 100 (capped). All three controllable staff have acted = false. Happy Hour is active on turns 7 and 8.
2. Host seats customer 3 — objects continue on the same lifelines.
seatCustomer(3, 1, StaffRole.HOST)
seatCustomer(customer3, table1)
Host inherits seatCustomer(...) from SeatingStaff and markActed() from ControllableStaff. These calls execute on the host object.
State: table1.occupant = customer3; customer3.status = SEATED; customer3 is removed from the waiting queue; host.acted = true.
3. Waiter takes the discounted order — objects continue on the same lifelines.
VIP calculation: (1800 × 9 + 5) / 10 = 1620 cents. Controller then applies Happy Hour: (1620 × 8 + 5) / 10 = 1296 cents (integer division).
[happyHourTurnsRemaining > 0] — controller applies the additional discount
«create» Order(pasta, 1296)
takeOrder(customer3, order3)
State: customer3.order = order3; order3 is PLACED with 0/2 units; finalPriceCents = 1296 ($12.96); waiter.acted = true. Customer remains SEATED.
4. First preparation unit and end of turn — objects continue on the same lifelines.
[else: acted = false] — alternative; Chef is not called
[acted = true] — selected; Chef and order eligibility checks succeed

endTurn() processes: payments → EATING customers → JUST_SERVED customers → satisfaction / abandonment → advanceTurn(). Customer 3 is SEATED, so only satisfaction / abandonment applies to this customer. Other customers are outside this trace.
End of Turn 7: currentTurn = 8; Happy Hour has 1 turn remaining; customer3 = SEATED, satisfaction = 95; order3 = PREPARING (1/2); table1 occupied; chef.acted = true.

How this implements the use case: GameCLI sends player choices to GameController. The controller coordinates objects; Host seats the customer, VIPCustomer supplies VIP pricing, the controller adds Happy Hour pricing, Waiter places the Order, and Chef advances preparation after Waiter has acted.

The selected path has acted = true. The alt fragment also shows the rejected preparation call when acted = false; this alternative does not occur in this run. Happy Hour bonus application normally iterates over customers; only customer 3 is expanded here. No loop is implied over this one customer.

Scope at endTurn(): payment → eating → just-served → satisfaction / abandonment → advanceTurn(). The supplied victory run also pays customer 2; that interaction is outside this customer-3 use case. Customer 3 remains SEATED until served and therefore loses 5 satisfaction points this turn.

Notation: solid filled arrow = synchronous call; dashed open arrow = reply or «create»; opt = conditional interaction; alt = mutually exclusive branches. State notes are not return values. Execution bars are omitted. Staff markActed() methods are inherited; the calls execute on the actual staff objects. Outcome applies after endTurn(), before Turn 8 startTurn(): satisfaction = 95; the next turn’s Happy Hour bonus has not yet been applied.
